reason: The text fragment from Exodus 1:15-22 describes Pharaoh's command to the Hebrew midwives to kill newborn Hebrew boys. The passage shows the midwives fearing God (Elohim) and disobeying Pharaoh's order, while God rewards the midwives and the Hebrew population multiplies. There is no indication of the Hebrew people blaming their leaders or Yahweh for the risk they face. Rather, the text portrays God favorably (dealing well with the midwives) and positions Pharaoh as the external threat. The narrative does not contain any expression of blame directed at either leadership or God from the Hebrew people.
